learn.title: Atoms
learn.body: An atom is the smallest unit of an element. Every element, like oxygen or gold, is made of its own kind of atom.

learn.title: Inside an atom
learn.body: The center, the nucleus, holds protons (positive) and neutrons (neutral). Electrons (negative) move around it.

learn.title: Molecules
learn.body: When two or more atoms bond together they form a molecule. Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom bond to make a water molecule, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

learn.title: Build a water molecule
learn.body: Follow the atoms as they bond.
steps: Take 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom.
You now have one water molecule, written $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

learn.body: Opposite charges attract. Protons (+) hold electrons (−) close, and neutrons add no charge at all.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest unit of an element?
questions.explanation: An atom is the smallest unit that still has the properties of its element.

questions.prompt: Match each particle with its charge.
questions.explanation: Protons and electrons carry opposite charges, neutrons carry none.

questions.prompt: Two or more atoms bonded together form a \_\_.
questions.explanation: Atoms joined by chemical bonds make a molecule.
